newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK invites over 60 Taiwanese to witness handover.
newsitem.headline: HK invites over 60 Taiwanese to witness handover.

text.p: Hong Kong has invited more than 60 Taiwanese to ceremonies marking its return to Chinese rule, but diplomatically-sensitive seating plans are giving organisers more headaches than a wedding banquet.

"Basically, we have issued over 60 invitations to people from Taiwan, they are being invited in their personal capacities," a radio station quoted Stephen Lam, director of the handover ceremonies, as saying.
With China also hosting, organisers are having trouble seating their guests from Taiwan, which Beijing views as a rebel province since a civil war split them in 1949.

"As for seating arrangements...if you have done wedding banquets for two or three hundred people, you know how difficult it is, and now we are trying to do one for 4,000 people," Lam said on Sunday after the inauguration of the press and broadcast centre for the handover.
More than 4,000 guests from around the world will attend the ceremonies to mark the territory's transition to Chinese soverignty at midnight on June 30, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
Taiwanese officials have said they would not witness the handover ceremony if their country was treated as another province of China.

"It is simply unacceptable if the (Taiwan) representatives are seated with the mainland's provincial representatives," Kao Koong-lian, vice-chairman of Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council, said last week.
Taipei maintains its Chinese Nationalist republic has equal status to that of China's Communist government.
Lam said he would not reveal the Taiwanese guest list before he received their replies.
The police say security will be super-tight to prevent trouble at the event, including guerrilla attacks or bomb scares.
But he also said the authorities would be tolerant of demonstrations during the celebration so long as they are peaceful and lawful.
"We welcome all lawful and peaceful demonstrations," Lee said.
